analysis.title: A few thouhts: PRY, STM, SZG, HLN
key_insights: Alphabet's Q3 missed in Search and YouTube, raising questions about AI monetization and FCF generation. Cloud demand was strong but margins only flat despite higher TPU sales. The author sees it as unhelpful for the AI theme and mostly negative for the GOOG business model.

Oracle shares rose 10% after market. Oracle expects FCF positive in H2 2028, two quarters earlier than Karl Keristead expected. Oracle says it can fund capex without additional debt or equity, and not by cutting AI investment, using more vendor financing, customer-owned chips and prepayments. The author sees this as supportive for the AI theme, for Oracle, and for indebted neoclouds like CoreWeave.

Prysmian (Buy) reported a Q3 beat and raise: revenue 7% above consensus, EBITDA 6% above consensus, driven by Transmission and electrification. Power Grid and Digital Solutions missed on top line and margins. FY26 FCF and EBITDA guidance was lifted to 6% and 10% ahead of consensus.

Prysmian shares have underperformed recently while earnings estimates keep rising. The author says the stock prices very little of its growth potential, with grid network and data-center fiber growth giving a good risk balance.

STMicro (Buy) is trading up slightly after in-line Q3 and a higher Q4 guide (Q3 sales +17.9% y/y, Q4 guided +24.7%). Gross margin beat in Q3 and is guided to 39% for Q4 vs consensus 38%. The Silicon Carbide repositioning against Chinese competitors has meant some double costs, which are now being resolved.

STM data-center revenue (silicon photonics, AI power semiconductors) is projected at about $2.5bn in 2027 (14% of group sales) and $3.8bn in 2028 (19%). STM holds 90% share in power semis at Starlink, about 6% of group sales this year. Industrials and Autos show signs of bottoming.
The near-term argument for STM is the recent AI-driven sell-off, which prices a negative value for its AI exposure. The author names STM and ASML as most attractive for an AI sentiment recovery.

Haleon (Buy) fell 13% on a weak Q3 trading update, back to 330p, where it was a month ago. Staples and pharma had benefited for 4-5 weeks from the AI sell-off, so part of the drop is a breather. Q3 volume/mix was +0.5% vs consensus +1.3% and Q2 +1.4%, due to a weaker cold and flu season (40bp hit) and discontinued OTC products in China. FY26 growth outlook was cut.

Haleon guides Q4 underlying organic growth of 4% and high-single-digit operating profit growth (constant FX, ex one-offs). The author suggests considering Haleon in place of ULVR, NESN and HENKEL positions after the sell-off.

Salzgitter rose 9% after raising its full-year EBITDA guide to EUR800-875mn from EUR725-825mn (consensus EUR741mn), with 9m sales of EUR7.3bn and sales guidance of EUR10bn confirmed. UBS analyst Andy Jones upgraded it to Buy on Oct 9 on EU steel import tariffs.

EU tariffs would cut steel imports to 18.3mt/year, with a 50% tariff above quota, removing about 9mt of annual imports. UBS expects European steel prices toward EUR900/t and 8-20% EBITDA upgrades. Price target for Salzgitter is EUR71, leaving upside after the 9% move.
